messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The GDU model in the FAKEDETECTOR framework accepts multiple inputs from different sources simultaneously, including extracted feature vectors from HFLU, and outputs its learned hidden state to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture." -- cites: E4 (Section C): quote "Formally, the GDU model accepts multiple inputs from different sources simultaneously, i.e., x i , z i and t i , and outputs its learned hidden state h i to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture."
2. "The GDU and HFLU modules in the FAKEDETECTOR framework are illustrated in Figure 5." -- cites: E1 (Figure 5): observation "The architecture of the FAKEDETECTOR framework is illustrated in Figure 5."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 5, page 7) (image attached): Fig. 5. The Architecture of Framework F AKE D ETECTOR .
Words printed in the figure: u1 HFLU GDU y Input HFLU GDU y Input u2 HFLU GDU y Input u3 HFLU GDU y Input HFLU GDU y Input HFLU GDU y Input HFLU GDU y Input n1 n2 n3 n4 HFLU GDU Input HFLU GDU Input HFLU GDU Input s1 s2 s3
[E4] (text, Section C, page 6): The overall architecture of F AKE D ETECTOR corresponding to the case study shown in Figure 3 is provided in Figure 5. Besides the HFLU feature learning unit model, F AKE D ETEC - TOR also uses a gated diffusive unit (GDU) model for effective relationship modeling among news articles, creators and subjects, whose structure is illustrated in Figure 4. Formally, the GDU model accepts multiple inputs from different sources simultaneously, i.e., x i , z i and t i , and outputs its learned hidden state h i to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture. Here, let’s take news articles as an example. Formally, among all the inputs of the GDU model, x i denotes the extracted feature vector from HFLU for news articles, z i represents the input from other GDUs corresponding to subjects, and t i represents the input from other GDUs about creators. Considering that the GDU for each news article may be connected to multiple GDUs of subjects and creators, the mean ( · ) of the outputs from the GDUs corresponding to these subjects and creators will be computed as the inputs z i and t i instead respectively, which is also indicated by the GDU architecture illustrated in Figure 4. For the inputs from the subjects, GDU has a gate called the “forget gate”, which may update some content of z i to forget. The forget gate is important, since in the real world, different news articles may focus on different aspects about the subjects and “forgetting” part of the input from the subjects is necessary in modeling. verdicts.reason: The cited evidence in E4 (Section C) mentions that the GDU model accepts inputs x_i, z_i, and t_i simultaneously, but it does not specify that these inputs are extracted feature vectors from HFLU. The claim also mentions that the GDU model outputs its learned hidden state to the output layer and other unit models in the diffusive network architecture, which is not directly supported by the evidence in E4.

The cited evidence in E1 (Figure 5) only illustrates the architecture of the FAKEDETECTOR framework and does not specifically mention the GDU and HFLU modules. The claim states that the GDU and HFLU modules are illustrated in Figure 5, which is not supported by the evidence.
